What’s inside

Four jobs. Fifty ready-made prompts.

Every prompt already has the role, the task, the shape and the limits built in — the parts a vague prompt leaves out. Tap a card to jump straight to that section of the list.

✕ The vague way

Write an email.

The AI has to guess who it’s for, what happened, and how it should sound — so it guesses safe and generic.

✓ Prompt No. 1 from the sheet

Write a short, friendly email to [name]. I’m going to be about [30 minutes] late because [traffic]. Say sorry once, keep it to 3–4 sentences, and say I’ll catch up today.

Same AI. Same task. You just took the guessing away. Copy this one →

How to use it

Three steps. Thirty seconds.

  1. 1

    Copy

    Pick the prompt that matches your job — on this page, or from the PDF. Don’t rewrite it from scratch; the wording is doing work for you.

  2. 2

    Fill the [brackets]

    Swap every [bracket] for your real detail. One sentence of background is often enough — more specific in, less generic out.

  3. 3

    Treat the first answer as a draft

    Then ask one follow-up: Make it shorter, Make it friendlier, or Cut the second paragraph. Good results usually show up on round two or three.

Before you hit enter

The 5-point check, on every prompt you write.

The 50 prompts have these built in. When you write your own, run down the list — missing one? Add one sentence. That’s usually enough.

Who?

Who is it for — and who should the AI act as?

What?

The exact task, in one clear sentence.

Background?

The situation it can’t see unless you type it.

Shape?

Email, table, 5 bullets, step-by-step — pick one.

Don’ts?

Limits: length, tone, what to leave out.

!

Before you send anything it writes

Check names, dates and numbers. AI sometimes fills gaps with a confident guess — if a date or a name wasn’t in your notes, don’t let it invent one.
